units: <cite ref="Targum Jonathan on II Kings 3:11">Targ. II Kings III, 11</cite>.
<cite ref="Targum Jonathan on I Kings 19:4">Targ. I Kings XIX, 4</cite>.
<cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Job 31:30">Targ. Job XXXI, 30</cite> <he>למִשְׁאַל</he> Ms. (ed. <he>למִשְׁיַיל</he>, <he>למִשְׁיַל</he>).
Targ. Y. Deut. I, 1 שַׁיְילְתוּן (ed. Vien. שַׁיְילַתַּוּן, read: שַׁיַּילְתּוּן, Pa).
<cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Psalms 137:3">Targ. Ps. CXXXVII, 3</cite>; a. fr.—<he>ש׳ לשלם</he>, <he>ש׳ בשלם</he>, v. <cite ref="U01351"><he>שְׁלָם</he></cite>.—
<cite ref="Shabbat 20b:2">Sabb. 20ᵇ</cite>; <cite ref="Shabbat 21a:3">21ᵃ</cite> <he>שְׁאִילְתִּינְהוּ לכל וכ׳</he>, v. <cite ref="N00484"><he>נָחוֹתָא</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Shabbat 30a:3">Ib. 30ᵃ</cite> <he>שׁאוּל שאילה זו וכ׳</he> they asked the following question &c., v. <cite ref="P00565"><he>עֵיל</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Taanit 21a:5">Taan. 21ᵃ</cite> <he>אי איכא דשָׁאֵיל לי וכ׳</he> if any one were to ask me a question from the Mishnah of &c.

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Sheviit 7:1:13">Y. Shebi. VII, 37ᶜ</cite> top <he>הא גברא מִישְׁאֲלִינֵיה אתא שַׁאֲלוּנֵיה וכ׳</he> (not <he>מישאלינית</he>) here is a man whom you night ask; he came, and they asked; a. fr.—Part. pass. <cite ref="U00023"><he>שְׁאִיל</he></cite>.

<cite ref="Shabbat 30b:2">Sabb. 30ᵇ</cite> <he>ולענין שאילה דשְׁאִילְנָא קדמיכון</he> and as to the question which I have been asked in your presence; [Rashi: <he>דשָׁאֵילְנָא</he> which I asked, a courteous phrase for ‘which you asked of me’]; a. e.
Targ. Ex. XXII, 13; a. fr.—[Targ. O. ib. XII, 36, v. infra Af.]—
<cite ref="Bava Metzia 97a:10">B. Mets. 97ᵃ</cite> <he>ההוא גברא דש׳ וכ׳</he> a man borrowed a cat from his neighbor &c.
<cite ref="Bava Metzia 97a:10">Ib.</cite> <he>האי … למִישְׁאַל מידי וכ׳</he> if one wishes to borrow an object from his neighbor and be free from responsibility for an accident &c.
<cite ref="Bava Metzia 97a:7">Ib.</cite> <he>נימא ליה שְׁאֵיל וכ׳</he> let him (the lender) say to him, first take what you want to borrow, and then &c.

<cite ref="Yevamot 120b:4">Yeb. 120ᵇ</cite> <he>לא שָׁיְילֵי</he> (not <he>שיולי</he>); <cite ref="Bava Metzia 27b:8">B. Mets. 27ᵇ</cite> <he>לא שְׁאִילֵי</he>, v. <cite ref="O01444"><he>סְקַב</he></cite>; a. fr.—Part. pass. as ab.

<cite ref="Bava Metzia 97a:10">Ib. 97ᵃ</cite> <he>שאיל לן מר</he> you (as teacher) are loaned to us, i.e. you are in our service, and if we borrow an object from you, we are not responsible, it being <he>שאילה בבעלים</he>, v. <cite ref="U00026"><he>שְׁאִילָה</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Bava Metzia 97a:10">Ib.</cite> <he>אתון שְׁאִילְתּוּן לי</he> you are in my service.

<cite ref="Bava Metzia 97a:10">Ib.</cite> <he>איהו ש׳ להו … אינהו שְׁאִילוּ ליה וכ׳</he> he (the teacher) is in their (the scholar’s) service on the Kallah day (v. <cite ref="K00691"><he>כַּלָּה</he></cite>); they are in his on any other day; a. e.—

<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 65:15">Gen. R. s. 65</cite> <he>לא שאיל הוא לה ולא שְׁאִילָה היא ליה</he> (some ed. <he>שאול … שאולה</he>) he is not loaned to her, nor she to him, i.e. the simile does not fit the application, nor the application the simile.
<cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Exodus 12:35">Targ. Y. Ex. XII, 35</cite>; a. e.—
<cite ref="Beitzah 19a:7">Bets. 19ᵃ</cite> <he>אתא … לשַׁיּוּלֵי וכ׳</he> he came before the Rabbis to ask &c.
<cite ref="Chullin 3b:10">Ḥull. 3ᵇ</cite> <he>דליתיה קמן דלִישַׁיְּילֵיה</he> when he is not before us so that we could ask him.
<cite ref="Tamid 32a:26">Tam. 32ᵃ</cite> <he>מְשַׁיַּילְנָא לכו</he> I am asking you; a. fr.
<cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Exodus 12:36">Targ. Y. Ex. XII, 36</cite>.—
<cite ref="Taanit 21b:4">Taan. 21ᵇ</cite>, v. <cite ref="G00037"><he>זְבִילָא</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Taanit 21b:8">Ib.</cite> <he>דמחממת … ומְשַׁיְּילָא וכ׳</he> who heated her oven and let her neighbors use it; a. fr.

<cite ref="Onkelos Exodus 12:36">Targ. O. Ex. XII, 36</cite> ed. Berl. (ed. Vien. <he>שאילינון</he>, corr. acc.); a. e.—Yeb. l. c. <he>ולא מוֹשְׁלֵי</he>, v. <cite ref="N00519"><he>נְחַשׁ</he> I</cite>.
<cite ref="Bava Metzia 116a:7">B. Mets. 116ᵃ</cite> <he>דעביד לאוֹשׁוּלֵי וכ׳</he> which it is customary to lend and hire out; a. e.
<cite ref="Targum Jonathan on I Samuel 20:6">Targ. I Sam. XX, 6</cite>.

senses.gloss: (with ב־) to allow one’s self to be inquired of; to answer, issue an oracle.
units: <cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Ezekiel 14:3">Targ. Ez. XIV, 3</cite>.
<cite ref="Targum Jerusalem, Numbers 24:1">Targ. Y. II, Num. XXIV, 1</cite>.
<cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Isaiah 65:1">Targ. Is. LXV, 1</cite>.

senses.gloss: (with ל־) to bring a case up for decision, to ask. Y. Maasr. II, beg. 49ᶜ אִשְׁתָּאֲלִית לאילין וכ׳ I asked those of the house of &c. Y. Sabb. XII, 13ᶜ bot., אִשְׁתַּאֲלַת לר׳ שמעון וכ׳ R. S. b. L. was asked. Ib. VI, 8ᵃ ואִיתְשְׁלַת לר׳ ומר וכ׳ when the case was brought before Rabbi, he said &c.; a. fr.—Esp. to come before a scholar for absolution from a vow.
units: <cite ref="Nedarim 90a:7">Ned. 90ᵃ</cite> <he>אי בעי על נדרו איתשיל ברישא וכ׳</he> if he so desires, he may ask first for absolution from his vow of abstinence, or if he chooses, he may ask first for absolution from his nazaritic vow; <cite ref="Nedarim 90a:4">ib.</cite> <he>נִיתְּשִׁיל</he>; a. fr.
